newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat steadies at expected turning point.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat steadies at expected turning point.

text.p: Australian wheat futures sold steady on Monday, poised at a crucial point where a break upward could spark price recovery or continued decline could produce offloading onto the market, brokers said.
November 1996 edged back by 50 cents to A$148.50 in three trades while January 1997 sold steady on A$149.50 in 23 trades.
Some recovery in prices had occurred and the threatened wheat subsidy war between the EU and the U.S. had receded, Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said.
"The market is poised at a crucial point. A fall from here would see a new wave of selling ... and also destroy the confidence that has been building up," Booth said.
But the tone of the market had changed, interest was high and technicals good, he said.

Many growers who had sold forward but would also hold stocks on farm in the hope of higher prices next year were checking option possibilities, he said. Processors who saw the market breaking upward were also interested in derivative insurance.
The market remained in its long bear trend but was close to a possible upward break, he said.
